- [USER] User asked about favorite examples of cover songs transformed into something new and unique.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant stated it does not have preferences or feelings but provided an example of "All Along the Watchtower" by Jimi Hendrix, originally written and performed by Bob Dylan.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant described Hendrix's version as a psychedelic rock masterpiece with his signature guitar style and distinctive vocal interpretation.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant noted that Hendrix's version became iconic, leading many to forget it was a cover song.
- [USER] User expressed surprise at not knowing Hendrix's version was a cover song.
- [USER] User inquired about other examples of cover songs that became more popular than the original.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided a list of cover songs that became more popular than the originals:

  2. "Hurt" by Johnny Cash (originally by Nine Inch Nails)
  3. "I Will Always Love You" by Whitney Houston (originally by Dolly Parton)
  4. "The Man Who Sold the World" by Nirvana (originally by David Bowie)
  5. "Tainted Love" by Soft Cell (originally by Gloria Jones)
- [USER] User expressed interest in learning that "I Will Always Love You" was a cover by Dolly Parton.
- [USER] User asked if there are any other popular songs that are actually covers.

  2. "Yesterday" by The Beatles (written by Paul McCartney, credited to Lennon-McCartney)
  3. "Blinded by the Light" by Manfred Mann's Earth Band (originally by Bruce Springsteen)
  4. "Twist and Shout" by The Beatles (originally by The Top Notes)
  5. "Nothing Compares 2 U" by Sinéad O'Connor (originally by Prince)
- [USER] User expressed surprise at "Yesterday" being written by Paul McCartney and not credited to Lennon-McCartney.
